svg.text: Глава 12 · Ethernet операторского класса
Олифер, 7-е изд. · RAG p0351:c01–p0360:c01 · PDF 351–360 · printed 350–359
1 · Why classic Ethernet is insufficient for a carrier
LAN Ethernet is cheap/simple, but historically offers best-effort forwarding only
Carrier use needs reliability · failover · scalability · manageability
Provider wants service delivery and possibly internal L2 transport
UNI defines customer/provider service attachment
Flat customer MAC/VLAN state is not a scalable provider-core model
2 · Carrier-grade gaps
Address-space separation → customer vs provider service identifiers
Traffic engineering → STP/RSTP gives limited path control
Fault tolerance → operator expects predictable fast protection
OAM → detect reachability, localize failure, measure delay/loss
These are service/control functions layered around Ethernet forwarding
3 · CFM: continuity and fault localization
MEP → maintenance endpoint, sends/receives CCM for a service
MIP → transit observation point, does not originate CCM in source model
Missing CCM beyond timeout → service connection considered failed
MIP visibility narrows failure to a segment between intermediate points
Nested maintenance levels isolate customer/provider/operator OAM scopes
CFM is active monitoring because protocol-generated frames are injected
4 · Performance and service visibility
Y.1731 → one-way delay · delay variation · frame loss
E-LMI → CE can query service state and parameters from provider edge
Physical Ethernet OAM → directly linked interface fault/loopback testing
Remote loopback returns received frames to the peer for line analysis
Source explicitly warns: loopback disrupts normal service
Treat loopback as maintenance action with rollback and post-check
5 · Provider Bridge / Q-in-Q
Customer keeps C-VID inside original frame
Ingress provider edge pushes outer S-VID service tag
Provider core forwards according to outer service context
Egress provider edge removes S-VID and restores customer frame view
VLAN-ID spaces separated, but customer MAC learning remains in PB source model
6 · Why provider Ethernet keeps evolving
PB limits → customer MAC scale · S-VID space · STP path control
PBB → full customer/provider address separation via Ethernet encapsulation
Source then points to MPLS-based EVPN / L2 MPLS VPN for large providers
This deployment statement is preserved as source-era context
No current-market inference is added under rag_only
Operational reading rule
A provider Ethernet incident is a service-path problem: UNI → OAM domain → provider tag/mapping → provider path → destination.
Use disruptive physical loopback only after continuity/mapping/path evidence justifies it and a maintenance window exists.
No executable vendor CLI is supplied by the chapter.
Part-III questions start at p0361:c01 · reading state unchanged · source findings recorded separately.
